thread:
IncidentBot: [PAGER] High error rate detected for prod inference in us-west-2a (usw2a). Automated page to @Aisha (oncall).
Aisha (oncall): Ack 1: I'm on it. Initial dashboards? Any customer-facing impact?
IncidentBot: Snapshot (3m):
```
error_5xx: 10.4% (normal <0.6%)
resolver_errors: 3200/min
kvcache_miss: +52%
conn_reset_rate: 220/s
p95_latency: 520ms
```
Aisha (oncall): Oof. @Priya can you tail runtime logs for kvcache/model load failures while I check instance/ENI metrics?
Priya (runtime): Tailing logs now. Repeating pattern: kvcache rebuilds failing due to DNS timeouts, runtime showing `i/o timeout` on grpc to kv-store. Example: 
```
2026-03-15T18:05:12Z runtime ERROR kvcache: rebuild failed: dns lookup timeout
2026-03-15T18:05:13Z runtime ERROR modelloader: shard-fetch tcp timeout
```
Priya (runtime): Model worker goroutines stuck waiting on network reads; stack traces point to socket waits rather than CPU.
Leo (network): From VPC/host metrics: ENI rx_queue drops spike aligned with the timeline. Also seeing elevated resolver response latency and SERVFAIL counts concentrated in usw2a. Could be AZ resolver or host-side driver issue causing packets to be dropped on transmit/receive.
Carlos (infra): Can you gather `ethtool -S` and `netstat -s` outputs from a representative host? If RX drops are hardware-related we should isolate.
Aisha (oncall): Running `kubectl get nodes -l az=usw2a -o wide` shows several nodes Ready False. Need to stop scheduling there. @RouterBot, can you enact a temporary routing policy to reduce new traffic to usw2a?
RouterBot: Starting policy change: route preference lowered to 0% for usw2a across inference-prod (canary id c-2201). New sessions will prefer usw2b/usw2c. Existing sticky sessions preserved.
IncidentBot: Canary telemetry (1m): traffic shift 15% -> usw2b. Initial error rates in usw2b steady.
Nina (support): Customer impact check: approx 4% of requests in the US region failed with timeouts; some customers reported degraded features and increased retries. Recommending a status page "Partial degradation in US-WEST inference (single AZ)".
Aisha (oncall): Agree publish. Also we'll open AWS case. Leo, can you collect ENI counters and packet captures?
Leo (network): Collecting tcpdump & counters, uploading to s3: s3://redwood-incident-captures/3788888888/. Opening AWS SR 6801122333 requesting NIC telemetry, host-level packet captures, and verification of AZ resolver health.
Carlos (infra): To avoid mass cache misses and thundering herd during failover, we'll stagger drains and set kvcache warmup to a longer TTL. Priya, can you apply backoff on kvcache regen?
Priya (runtime): On it. Increasing regen backoff and gating model loads with a small randomized jitter. Also enabling degraded-mode to prefer smaller model variants for a short window to reduce network egress.
Aisha (oncall): We'll scale up capacity in other AZs. Carlos, please provision additional nodes in usw2b/usw2c and route new traffic there.
Carlos (infra): Spinning up 12 nodes across usw2b/usw2c, adjusting autoscaler min for inference-prod. Will coordinate with Priya to warm caches before routing large volumes.
RouterBot: Routing change progressed to 45% -> usw2b/usw2c per Aisha. Canary id c-2201 updated.
IncidentBot: Metrics after partial shift:
```
usw2a 5xx_rate: 3.1% (was 10.4%)
usw2b 5xx_rate: 0.2%
global p95: 360ms (was 520ms)
```
Nina (support): Draft status page: "Investigating partial degradation in inference for US-WEST. Traffic is being rerouted away from the affected availability zone while we work with the cloud provider. Some users may experience timeouts or higher latency." Approve?
Aisha (oncall): Approve; publish once AWS SR is referenced.
Leo (network): AWS responded: initial review shows NIC interrupts rising and possible offload regression on instances in usw2a. They asked to remove problematic AZ resolver endpoint from resolver pool temporarily. Requesting confirmation to proceed.
Aisha (oncall): Approve removal if AWS confirms it won't break internal services. Carlos, can you update resolver config for inference hosts to avoid the troubled resolver endpoint?
Carlos (infra): Pushing resolver config change to inference fleet to exclude that resolver IP. Also standing up ephemeral NAT gateways in other AZs to smooth egress during the shift in case resolver path was causing retries.
Priya (runtime): After reconfig and draining two hosts (staggered), kvcache miss rate fell and socket errors decreased significantly. Runtime load looks stable on replacement nodes.
Aisha (oncall): Handing incident to Carlos for night shift and AWS follow-up. I'll write initial notes for the post-incident review. Please keep channel updates and tag me for rollback approval if we want to rejoin usw2a.
Carlos (infra): Taking ownership. AWS SR 6801122333 remains open; will request driver/firmware checks and a postmortem from provider if hardware/firmware implicated. Creating incident ticket INC-2026-089 for root cause analysis and follow-ups.
Nina (support): Status update posted and customers with high touch flagged for direct outreach. Preparing postmortem comms template.
IncidentBot: Incident state: mitigation active, traffic partially rerouted, ENI drops and resolver failures correlated, AWS engaged. Next automated snapshot in 20 minutes.
Aisha (oncall): Good job team. Once AWS confirms resolver/NIC health and we see stable telemetry for 2h, we'll consider controlled failback. :white_check_mark:
Carlos (infra): Follow-ups include: add playbook for single-AZ resolver removal, improve kvcache warmup behavior to reduce failover pain, and add automated ENI health checks to our monitoring.
Nina (support): Adding impacted customer list to the incident ticket for outreach.
IncidentBot: Thread closed for now; updates will be posted in INC-2026-089.
